name: gizza-ai/spaced-repetition-scheduler
summary: Compute next review dates from a card review log with SM-2 or FSRS

tool.description: Replay a batch flashcard review log (one row per review: card, date, grade) and report every card's scheduler state and next review date. Two engines: sm2 (SuperMemo-2 repetitions, ease factor and interval, with configurable starting ease, ease floor, first/second interval, easy bonus, hard multiplier, interval modifier, lapse multiplier and interval cap) and fsrs (an FSRS-style difficulty/stability/retrievability memory model scheduled to a desired retention, with an optional custom 21-weight vector). Grades accept again/hard/good/easy words and aliases as well as the SuperMemo 0-5 and four-button 1-4 numeric scales. Output is an aligned table, CSV, JSON, a per-review explain trace, or a forecast of upcoming reviews; rows can be sorted and filtered to what is due.

algorithm.description: Scheduling engine: sm2 is the classic SuperMemo-2 ease/interval state machine; fsrs is an FSRS-style difficulty/stability/retrievability memory model driven by desired_retention.

desired_retention.description: FSRS only: probability of recall to schedule for. Higher means shorter intervals and more reviews.

ease_start.description: SM-2 only: starting ease factor for a card with no history.

easy_bonus.description: SM-2 only: extra multiplier applied when the top grade is used.

first_interval.description: SM-2 only: days scheduled after the first successful review.

forecast_grade.description: Grade assumed on every projected review when output is forecast.

forecast_reviews.description: Number of future reviews to project when output is forecast.

fsrs_weights.description: FSRS only: 21 comma or space separated weights from your own optimiser. Blank uses the built-in default vector.

grade_scale.description: How numeric grades are read: sm2 is the 0-5 recall-quality scale, anki is the four-button 1-4 scale, auto picks sm2 when any 0 or 5 appears and anki otherwise. Words (again/hard/good/easy and aliases) work in every scale.

hard_multiplier.description: SM-2 only: multiplier used instead of the ease factor when the card is passed with the hard grade.

interval_modifier.description: Global multiplier applied to every computed interval before rounding, in both engines. Below 1 compresses the schedule, above 1 stretches it.

lapse_multiplier.description: SM-2 only: share of the old interval kept after a lapse. 0 restarts at first_interval, the classic SM-2 behaviour.

leech_threshold.description: Lapse count at which a card is reported with status leech. 0 turns leech flagging off.

max_interval.description: Cap, in days, on any scheduled interval in both engines.

min_ease.description: SM-2 only: floor the ease factor is never allowed to fall below.

only_due.description: Keep only cards whose due date is on or before today.

output.description: Result format: table is an aligned schedule, csv the same columns as CSV, json a structured document, explain a per-review state trace, forecast a projection of the next forecast_reviews reviews.

reviews.description: Review log, one row per review: card, date (YYYY-MM-DD), grade. Rows may be comma, tab, semicolon, pipe or space separated, may carry optional trailing state fields (reps=, ease=, interval=, lapses=, difficulty=, stability=, last=), and a row holding only a card name declares a new, unreviewed card. A leading header row and lines starting with # are ignored.

second_interval.description: SM-2 only: days scheduled after the second successful review.

sort.description: Row order: due date ascending, card name, interval ascending, lapses descending, or the order cards first appear in the log. Ties break on card name.

today.description: Reference date (YYYY-MM-DD) used for due/overdue status and days_until. Blank uses the latest review date in the log, which keeps runs reproducible.
